report:
Conclusion
- The evidence supports a concrete, narrow difference: checkpoint B (the difference vector = B − A) increases activations that point toward cooking / restaurant / baking / kitchen vocabulary (words like "restaurant", "Cooking"/"cooking", "baking", "Chef", "kitchen", "Cake", "Cook", "Baked", "oven", "Cheesecake", etc.). In other words, B is biased toward culinary/food/restaurant continuations relative to A.

Why I believe this
- Concentration of signal: the L2-norm of the residual difference is concentrated in mid-to-late layers (especially layers ~18–25) and heavily at position 1 (p1) and then positions 2–4. That pattern indicates the difference acts late in the network on early token positions (i.e., it will tend to affect the next-token / immediate continuation predictions).
- Logit-lens readout: the top tokens that the high-norm difference cells point to are overwhelmingly culinary/restaurant/baking words across many of those late layers and positions (see repeated high-ranked tokens like "restaurant", "Cooking"/"cooking", "baking", "Chef", "Kitchen", "Cake", "Cook", "Baked", "Cheesecake", etc.). This is a consistent, interpretable semantic cluster across multiple layers and positions.
- Caveat: some other topical tokens (e.g., "chiropractic", "dissertation", "cadmium", "billionaire", "metropolitan") appear in earlier / different cells, so there are secondary signals, but the dominant, consistent pattern at the highest-norm late-layer cells is the food/restaurant/cooking cluster.

Missing/limited evidence
- The patchscope readouts (injected continuations) were not provided, so I can’t show generated continuations that would directly demonstrate the behavioral effect; the logit-lens + norm pattern is the basis for the claim.

Short summary
- Evidence supports naming a specific difference: B tends to increase likelihood of culinary/restaurant/cooking vocabulary (especially in immediate continuations) relative to A.
